b:
Ekam sat; viprā bahudhā vadanti

My mother is devout.. I am the one who dived and bathed in that flood of devotion.. Even our family trips were temple trips.. Collecting holy ash at every temple, bathing in the sacred tanks, buying idols: ours was a family that grew its devotion by bribing every branch without grudge, Shaiva, Vaishnava, Shakta, Skanda, Ganapatya..

To my mother, even Mother Mary is simply Mariamman

In our house there is a place for the baby Jesus too. The Quran is respected too. The Buddha is welcome too

God exists. That is certain.. That alone is my mother's creed.. I grew up following in her footsteps. At least once a month, the temple. A calling card to God, given in my name. That I and those close to me may be well, that I alone may stand in front as first in class, that the times tables I learned by heart may not be forgotten: I had countless small-change prayers.. And for them, countless offerings, from the 5 rupees dropped in the hundi to steamed kozhukattai..

The prime mover of all this was our IBC Pillaiyar.. In those days he was widely praised as the Visa Pillaiyar. Countless people made vows and won visas.. There are stories of applications the embassy rejected being accepted higher up by the grace of Visa Pillaiyar.. In time, as the war ended and the need for visas fell, Pillaiyar's customers dwindled.. But the old-timers, not forgetting the old ways, still never begin their day without seeing the puja of the Pillaiyar who sits there gracefully at that street corner, gazing at the western beach

Later, as I grew up, Pillaiyar too became a minor god.. The big temples drew me, and the one I clung to was the Aishwarya Lakshmi temple

The goddess, seated six feet tall with a calm smile and, along with it, a hint of sorrow, gives me goosebumps.. She gives whatever you ask, at once.. I prayed and got into medicine. Later, though I prayed many times that I didn't want it, she stayed stone and never took it back

Whether God exists, I do not know.. But in her I see my mother.. Like my mother, she gives if you ask.. She listens to my babbling. She sends someone to wipe away my tears.

These days when I go to the temple I don't join my palms in worship. I don't make archanai offerings.. I talk with her and come away..

She too will be waiting for me to come back and talk again, like my mother
note: The opening is from the Rig Veda: "Truth is one; the wise call it by many names." Mariamman is a Tamil mother goddess. A hundi is a temple offering box; kozhukattai are steamed sweet dumplings offered to Pillaiyar (Ganesha). An archanai is a priest-led offering of praise in the worshipper's name.
